subject: Compare expected mean shape using pairwise

messages.author: 6180ccabbdf86586
messages.subject: Compare expected mean shape using pairwise
parts:
I have shape data for individuals aged 6, 7, and 10 years, which includes both sexes. I performed fit1 <- lm.rrpp(shape ~ sex*age) and want to test for statistical signiciance of shape differences of the expected mean shape between sexes at each age group. Here is how I did it:

gp <- interaction(sex, age)
pw <- pairwise(fit1, groups = gp)
summary(pw, confidence = 0.95, test.type = "dist")

This will return significance of shape differences at ages 6, 7, and 10 years. Since I have established a linear model of shape and age, I am also interested in predicting shape at ages 8 and 9, and compare sexual dimorphism of shapes at these two ages. Is there a way to do this in geomorph/RRPP?

A solution is to permute group labels 1000 times and run lm.rrpp with iter=1 each time. This will create a distribution of Procrustes distance at whichever ages of interest and just calculate the number of times the permuted PD is larger than the observed (i.e., p value). Please let me know if this is a valid alternative. But I do want to do this inside geomorph/RRPP.

Thank you.
Kieran

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Compare expected mean shape using pairwise
parts:
Kieran,

 

If you treated age as a continuous variable in your linear model, then you can easily predict the shape at other ages. Please see the help page for the function ‘shape.predictor’. It has examples for quite a few scenarios, including regression (the ‘allometry example’ in the help file).

 

Dean

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Compare expected mean shape using pairwise
parts:
The RRPP::predict function can also be useful for putting confidence intervals on predictions, especially when predictions are different than fitted values.  The function requires making a data frame for “new data” (which can be in part training data, also), which can be a little tricky.  The vignette for using RRPP has some examples to demonstrate its use.

Mike
